rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3-4 and Tables 3-5 report the authors' own model training and evaluation runs (modified MobileNetV2 with SE blocks and residual skip connections) on 87,000+ PlantVillage leaf images, reaching 0.98 accuracy and 0.98 F1 on a held-out test set, plus an ablation study.
rows.notes: The study classifies close-up RGB leaf images from the public PlantVillage dataset (Mohanty et al., 2016) into 38 healthy/diseased classes; it does not use UAV or any remote-sensing imagery, so the technology is not the one the review context attributes (drone/remote sensing). It reports classification accuracy per class (including tomato/potato late blight and corn/apple rust) but does not grade infection severity, does not test detection before canopy-wide or visible symptoms (images show visible symptoms), and does not evaluate any targeted response or disease control outcome; claims about enabling early intervention and crop protection are assertions, not results. Detection is a precondition of the claimed control function, so Q2 is no and upstream is true. Per-class precision/recall are reported but no dispersion measures; limitations noted (data imbalance, interpretability) concern the classifier, not the claimed effect.

notes: Full text appears complete. Minor internal inconsistency: abstract/discussion report 98% accuracy while the conclusion states 96%.
